1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif at comfortable size with generous line spacing and clear headings, though secrets and log output are in dense monospace.

2.why: No italics or all-caps body text (only small 'SECURITY CENTRE' eyebrow label), and paragraphs are short, but the black Logs panel on every screen is a dense block of monospace text.

3.why: The layout is a single narrow centred column with full-width stacked buttons and inputs that reads well at phone width, although the 32-character setup secret and wide log lines risk overflow/tiny wrapping.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Enter the six-digit code generated during setup' and 'Use an authenticator app to generate time-based verification codes' are short and plain, with only mild jargon ('short-lived challenge', 'controlled test mode').

5.why: Placeholders show expected formats for mobile number (+15551234567) and recovery code (ABCD-EFGH-JKLM), but the identity verification code and authenticator code fields have no example or format hint.

6.why: Most steps need only a sentence or two, but the login screen's demo notice is a four-line paragraph and the persistent Logs panel grows to 25+ lines that the user must scan to find codes in test mode.

7.why: No copy button or copy affordance is shown anywhere — the 32-character manual setup secret and the recovery codes are plain text that must be transcribed by hand.

8.why: Step 5 explicitly offers only a 'Manual setup secret' with instruction to 'add it manually to your authenticator app'; no QR code or otpauth link is provided.

9.why: Fields are standard labelled inputs that a password manager could see, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete attributes (e.g. one-time-code) or password-manager/autofill support in the screenshots.

10.why: Each screen has one large bold heading and a single prominent filled blue primary button, though there is no step indicator such as 'Step 2 of 5'.

11.why: Steps 4–8 each ask for one action, but the login screen requires three fields plus two competing buttons, and the MFA settings screen presents generate/verify/log out actions together.

12.why: Confirmations like 'Setup secret generated. Enter it manually in your authenticator app.' and 'Enrolment confirmed. Your authenticator and recovery codes are active.' state what happened and often the next step.

13.why: 'Back to setup' / 'Back to MFA settings' links, 'Get a simulation challenge' re-request, and 'Generate replacement codes' allow retry, but there is no reveal/hide toggle for the secret or codes and replacement permanently invalidates prior codes.

14.why: No error state is shown in any of the 14 screenshots, so the claim cannot be confirmed; only success and informational messages are visible.

15.why: No countdown timer or session-expiry warning appears on any screen, but the copy mentions a 'short-lived challenge' and TOTP codes are inherently time-limited, with no stated generous allowance.
